blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Pressure is defined as force per unit area (P = F/A) and decreases as contact surface area increases.
Pressure in liquids increases linearly with depth, liquid density, and acceleration due to gravity.
Atmospheric pressure is exerted by the weight of air above and decreases with increasing altitude.
Archimedes' Principle states that a body submerged in a fluid experiences an upward buoyant force equal to the weight of displaced fluid.
Law of Floatation: An object floats if its average density is less than or equal to the density of the fluid.

blocks.content: Pressure is defined as the force acting per unit area.
It tells us how much force is applied on a particular area. Formula:
SI Unit of Pressure = Pascal (Pa) 1 Pascal = 1 Newton / m²

items: A sharp knife cuts easily because it has small area → more pressure.
A camel walks easily on sand because it has broad feet → less pressure.
High-heeled shoes exert more pressure than flat shoes.

blocks.content: If area is less → pressure is more If area is more → pressure is less
Liquids also exert pressure. Important points:

items:
• Liquid pressure increases with depth
  • Liquid pressure acts in all directions
  • Liquid pressure depends on height of liquid column
Liquid pressure acts in all directions
Liquid pressure depends on height of liquid column

blocks.content: The pressure exerted by air on the surface of the Earth is called atmospheric pressure. We do not feel atmospheric pressure because it acts equally in all directions.

items:
• Drinking with straw
  • Sucker sticking to wall
  • Collapse of empty bottle

blocks.content: The upward force exerted by a liquid on an object immersed in it is called buoyant force. This force helps objects to float.

rows: Exerted primarily downward in the direction of weight/applied force
Exerted equally in all directions at a specific depth (Pascal's Law)
P = h × ρ × g (Depth × Density × Gravity)
Depends on the contact surface area of the solid body
Independent of the shape or size of the container

blocks.content: When a body is immersed partially or completely in a fluid, it experiences an upward force equal to the weight of the fluid displaced.
This principle explains why objects float or sink.
An object floats or sinks depending upon its density.
If density of object < density of liquid → object floats If density of object > density of liquid → object sinks
Density is defined as mass per unit volume. Formula:
Density = Mass / Volume SI unit = kg/m³
Objects with higher density sink in water.

items:
• Broad tyres used in heavy vehicles
  • Sharp knives and needles
  • Dam walls thicker at bottom
  • Snow shoes used in snow regions
Broad tyres used in heavy vehicles
Snow shoes used in snow regions
Lactometers (milk purity test) and Hydrometers (fluid density) directly operate on Archimedes' Principle.
A sudden drop in a mercury barometer reading indicates an impending storm or cyclone.
Dams are constructed with broader bases because fluid pressure increases with depth (P = hρg).

blocks.content: Q1. SI unit of pressure? Ans: Pascal
Q2. Formula of pressure? Ans: Force / Area
Q3. Why do ships float? Ans: Due to buoyant force
Q4. Principle of flotation is based on? Ans: Archimedes’ principle
Q5. Pressure increases with? Ans: Depth

items:
• Pressure = Force / Area
  • Liquid pressure increases with depth
  • Atmospheric pressure surrounds Earth
  • Buoyant force acts upward
  • Archimedes principle explains floating
  • Density decides floating or sinking
